field.title: Fashion
field.description: A controlled vocabulary for the fashion domain — design, business, and communication — modelled as SKOS concept schemes with an optional CIDOC-CRM mapping layer.

subfields.title: Fashion Business
subfields.description: Sourcing, production economics, retail operations, distribution models, and sustainability governance.

concepts.definition: The process of identifying, vetting, and contracting suppliers of fabric, trims, and manufacturing capacity for production.
The full sequence of entities and processes — raw material, manufacture, logistics, retail — through which a garment moves from fiber to consumer.
The ability to track a garment's materials and production steps back through the supply chain, typically for compliance, sustainability, or authenticity claims.
A business model in which one company controls multiple stages of the supply chain — e.g. manufacturing and retail — rather than outsourcing them.
Merchandise manufactured by a third party but sold under a retailer's own brand name rather than the manufacturer's.
An agreement allowing a manufacturer to produce and sell goods under a designer's or brand's name in exchange for royalties, common in fragrance, eyewear, and accessories.
Selling goods in bulk to retailers at a discounted per-unit price, for onward resale to consumers, as distinct from direct-to-consumer selling.
A distribution model in which a brand sells directly to end customers, bypassing wholesale intermediaries, typically via owned e-commerce or retail.
The retail function of selecting and ordering product from suppliers for a store or platform, balancing trend, margin, and forecasted demand.
A budgeting tool that sets the dollar amount a buyer has available to purchase new inventory within a given period, based on planned sales, stock, and markdowns.
The planning and management of product assortment, pricing, and presentation to maximize sales across a retail season.
Determining the mix, depth, and breadth of styles, sizes, and colors a retailer will carry for a given season or store.
The amount added to a garment's cost price to set its retail price, usually expressed as a percentage or multiplier (e.g. "2.5x cost").
The difference between selling price and cost, expressed as a percentage of the selling price; the core profitability metric in fashion retail.
A reduction in a product's retail price, applied to move slow-selling stock and recover cash flow before a season closes.
The percentage of received inventory sold within a given period, a key indicator of how well a style or collection is performing.
The smallest quantity of a style a manufacturer will agree to produce in a single order, a key constraint for small and emerging brands.
The elapsed time between placing a production order and receiving finished goods, a critical planning variable across sourcing and buying.
A business model built on rapid design-to-shelf turnaround and frequent new-product drops, prioritizing speed and trend responsiveness over durability.
A production and consumption philosophy emphasizing durability, ethical labor, and reduced volume, positioned as a counter-model to fast fashion.
A model designed to keep garments and materials in use through resale, rental, repair, and recycling, minimizing the flow of virgin material in and waste out.
The sale of previously owned garments through dedicated platforms or brand-run take-back programs.
A model in which consumers pay to borrow garments for a limited period rather than purchase them outright.
Practices intended to reduce the environmental and social impact of fashion production and consumption across the product lifecycle.
Third-party verification that a product, material, or facility meets defined environmental or labor standards (e.g. GOTS, Fair Trade, Bluesign).
A contractual arrangement letting an independent operator run a store under a brand's name and system in exchange for fees, common for market entry in new territories.
A space, physical or digital, where a brand presents its collection to wholesale buyers and press for ordering and coverage decisions.
A scheduled industry event where multiple brands present collections to buyers, press, and other trade professionals under one roof.
Launching a new product category (e.g. fragrance, homeware) under an existing brand name to leverage its recognition into adjacent markets.
The sale of fashion goods through digital storefronts, encompassing owned websites, marketplaces, and social commerce.
The segment of the fashion industry producing high-volume, lower-priced goods for the broadest possible consumer base.

subfields.title: Fashion Communication
subfields.description: Brand identity, editorial and press practice, styling, events, and digital/social communication.

concepts.definition: The consistent set of visual, verbal, and experiential signals — logo, typography, color, tone — through which a fashion brand is recognized.
The characteristic style, vocabulary, and attitude a brand uses in written and spoken communication across all channels.
The codified visual system — logo, color palette, typography, photography style — applied consistently across a brand's touchpoints.
The overarching story a brand tells about its origin, values, and purpose, used to give coherence to campaigns and product launches.
The creative oversight of a campaign, shoot, or show's visual execution — casting, set, lighting, composition — to realize a defined concept.
A coordinated set of images, film, and messaging produced to promote a collection or brand moment across paid and owned media.
concepts.crm_mapping: crm:E7_Activity (the production process); outputs are crm:E31_Document / crm:E38_Image

concepts.definition: A curated set of photographs presenting a collection's key looks, used by press, buyers, and consumers to preview a season.
A styled photographic feature published in a magazine or online platform, built around a concept rather than direct product promotion.
Selecting and combining garments, accessories, and props to create a specific look for a shoot, show, or personal client.
One-to-one styling services provided to an individual client for their wardrobe or a specific occasion, as distinct from editorial or show styling.
A live presentation in which models walk a defined path wearing a collection's looks in sequence, for press, buyers, and increasingly livestream audiences.
A collection preview format in which looks are shown on stationary models or mannequins for guests to view at their own pace, as an alternative to a runway show.
A scheduled series of runway shows and presentations held in a given city, at which brands unveil upcoming seasonal collections to press and buyers.
A packaged set of materials — images, product details, brand background — distributed to journalists to support coverage of a launch or collection.
A formal written announcement distributed to media to communicate news — a launch, partnership, or appointment — in a brand's official framing.
Sending product to press, stylists, or influencers without charge in the hope of earning organic coverage or wear.
Paid or gifted partnerships with individuals who have an established audience, used to promote product or brand messaging through their own channels.
An individual, often a public figure, contracted to represent a brand publicly and consistently over an extended period, beyond a single campaign.
The seating position closest to the runway at a fashion show, reserved for top editors, buyers, celebrities, and VIP guests as a visible signal of status and access.
The design of in-store and window displays to present product attractively and guide customer movement and purchase decisions.
A curated arrangement of product and props in a store's street-facing window, used as a brand's most public communication surface.
A short film produced to communicate a brand's aesthetic and narrative, distinct from a straightforward product advertisement.
The integration of purchasing directly into social media platforms, collapsing discovery and checkout into a single interaction.
Photos, videos, or reviews created by consumers rather than the brand, often reshared as a lower-cost, higher-trust form of social proof.
A limited joint project between two brands, or a brand and an individual creative, that combines both names' identities into a distinct co-branded release.
A brand communication and design commitment to offering and representing an extended range of body sizes across product and campaign imagery.
A brand's use of its own history, archive, and founding narrative as a communication asset to establish authenticity and longevity.
A brand's or institution's preserved collection of historical garments, sketches, and documents, maintained for reference, exhibition, and heritage communication.
concepts.crm_mapping: crm:E78_Curated_Holding (a collection curated and maintained as a unit)

subfields.title: Fashion Design
subfields.description: Garment construction, pattern-making, materials, and the creative development process from concept to finished collection.

concepts.definition: The overall outer contour of a garment or outfit, independent of surface detail, fabric, or color.
concepts.scope_note: A vocabulary term used across design and buying to communicate shape quickly ("boxy silhouette," "hourglass silhouette") without reference to fabrication.

concepts.definition: A silhouette that narrows at the shoulders and flares gradually toward the hem, tracing the shape of the letter A.
A close-fitting silhouette that follows the body's natural line from shoulder to hem with minimal flare.
A silhouette with the waistline raised to sit just below the bust, with fabric falling loosely from that seam to the hem.
The technical process of translating a design sketch or draped form into flat templates ("pattern pieces") used to cut fabric.
Shaping fabric directly on a dress form or body to develop a pattern or silhouette by eye, rather than drafting flat.
A trial garment made in inexpensive fabric to test and refine a pattern before cutting the final material.
A basic, fitted pattern template without seam allowances or style lines, used as the foundation for developing new patterns.
Proportionally scaling a finished pattern up or down to produce the full range of garment sizes.
concepts.scope_note: Distinct from "fitting" — grading is mathematical scaling, not on-body adjustment.

concepts.definition: A session in which a garment sample is tried on a model or form to assess and correct fit, proportion, and ease.
How closely and comfortably a garment conforms to the body at key measurement points; a core quality attribute in both design and merchandising.
concepts.scope_note: In business use, "fit issues" are a leading cause of returns — see fashion_business.sellThrough.

concepts.definition: The difference between body measurements and garment measurements, added for comfort (wearing ease) or stylistic volume (design ease).
A stylized, elongated figure template used as the base for sketching fashion designs quickly.
A precise, proportionate line drawing of a garment shown without a body, used to communicate construction detail to a pattern maker or factory.
The complete production document set for a garment — flats, measurements, materials, trims, and construction notes — sent to a manufacturer.
An itemized list of every fabric, trim, and component required to construct a garment, with quantities and suppliers.
The specific fabric or material selected to execute a design, and the design decisions that follow from that choice (drape, hand, weight).
Any woven, knitted, or non-woven material produced from fibers, used as the raw substrate of a garment.
The tactile quality of a fabric — how it feels to the touch (soft, crisp, slippery, dry) — used as a technical descriptor in fabric sourcing.
How a fabric falls and moves under its own weight when hung or worn, a key criterion in fabric-to-silhouette matching.
A cohesive group of garments and accessories designed and produced together around a shared concept, palette, and season.
concepts.crm_mapping: crm:E65_Creation (as the creative process) — the resulting garments are individually crm:E22_Human-Made_Object

concepts.definition: A small, tightly edited collection of interchangeable pieces designed to mix and match, often released outside the main seasonal calendar.
A predictive report on upcoming color, fabric, silhouette, and cultural directions, produced ahead of a season to guide design and buying decisions.
The coordinated set of colors chosen to run across a collection or a single style, developed to reinforce a season's concept.

Legally protected French term for custom-fitted, hand-made garments produced by houses officially recognized by the Fédération de la Haute Couture et de la Mode, meeting strict criteria on atelier size and made-to-order production.
concepts.scope_note: Frequently misused generically for "expensive" or "high-end"; the term has a defined legal meaning in France.
concepts.crm_mapping: crm:E55_Type (a type of production, applied via crm:P2_has_type to the relevant crm:E12_Production)

concepts.definition: Garments manufactured in standard sizes and produced in quantity for direct retail sale, as opposed to made-to-measure.
The workshop where a design house's garments are constructed, historically distinguishing "flou" (soft dressmaking) from "tailleur" (tailoring) ateliers.
concepts.crm_mapping: crm:E53_Place (as the workshop location) — the working group itself is crm:E74_Group

concepts.definition: A reference table of body and garment measurements for each size in a brand's range, used to standardize fit across production.
A pattern-making approach that uses the entire width of fabric with no offcuts, integrating waste elimination into the cut itself rather than treating it as a post-production concern.

provenance.method: Curriculum-local YAML snapshot compiled from lexfield; definitions authored as controlled-vocabulary entries with optional CIDOC-CRM class mappings where heritage-relevant.
provenance.prototype_note: The fashion field is the seed tenant of lexfield; other fields (e.g. creativity_techniques) reuse the same Field→Subfield→Concept schema.
